tb21_profile.skill: Read an unfamiliar ontology out of a Turtle file and express a multi-hop, multi-criteria question as one declarative query: joins across professor-department-university-country, a COUNT DISTINCT threshold, membership in a hand-supplied set, and GROUP_CONCAT aggregation
tb21_profile.domain: RDF / Turtle / SPARQL knowledge graphs; adjacent territory is analytic SQL over a relational schema
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: the artifact is a single query file with a prescribed SELECT signature

verifier_notes: task_02500 (Terminal-Lego, ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY) and tw_455191 / tw_191978 (TerminalWorld joins) are FREE and are ranked in per_source only. notes: TMax is genuinely strong here - it has a real RDF/SPARQL family (rdflib, Jena, Turtle graphs, fixing a cross-joined SPARQL query) that retrieval had mostly buried; four of the final ten are TMax. CalibForge adds the single closest task in the whole pool (a SPARQL query over a Turtle org ontology written to /app/solution.sparql) plus a large data-querying family whose deliverable is likewise one saved declarative query with threshold, reference-date and recursion clauses, so it takes six slots. Terminal-Lego contributes nothing about RDF and only pandas-level filtering and joining; its ten are honest but weak (mostly 2s). TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis could not field ten defensible candidates either - their query content is schema creation, KSQL join snippets and table dumps, and their two best joins are FREE and absent respectively. SWE-Smith's value is SQL/Turtle parsers (pygments' Turtle lexer is the only RDF-syntax task outside TMax/CalibForge); SWE-Rebench offers only query-adjacent library bugs and scores low on task_form as expected.
